news.title: Linear Sells AI at Cost. Here’s Why.
news.gist: Linear keeps charging per seat and bills its agents’ model tokens at the provider’s rate with no markup, which Litterst says speeds up agent adoption but leaves little room for revenue to grow unless Linear starts charging for control.
points: Everyday agent work sits inside the seat; opt-in credits cover only Coding Sessions and background Loops
Credits are a shared dollar balance that rolls over and lapses a year after purchase, with no refunds or bulk discount
Selling at cost shuts down discount haggling, since any discount would mean a loss
The suggested fix: keep tokens at cost and charge for oversight, such as which agent can touch which code
nums: share of work in Linear created by AI agents, against 3% a year earlier
Linear’s net revenue retention on seat pricing
typical cost of one Loops run
yearly cost of 100 people on Business, which the author calls a low ceiling
news.why: If a vendor says its AI is sold at cost, check whether compute and background jobs carry the same promise, because Linear’s pledge covers only model tokens.

news.title: Slack moved Slackbot to tiered usage limits
news.gist: Slack dropped Slackbot’s ‘personal AI agent’ pitch for plan-by-plan quotas, and PricingSaaS reads the Business+ cap as a gate that pushes heavy AI users toward Enterprise+ rather than as a new charge.
points: Free and Pro use is consumption based, while Enterprise+ is unlimited
No new price was published, and the page doesn’t say whether messages stop or just slow at the cap
It came days after Slack’s Enterprise+ price display flipped back to contact sales in a live A/B test
Recent Slack changes also added paid Success Plans and a paid Frontline teams add-on
nums: Slackbot messages per Business+ user each week
real pricing-page changes Pulse has tracked at Slack since Jun 2023
60 days
Slack’s average gap between pricing changes
news.why: Business+ teams that lean on Slackbot for drafting or search should count their weekly use before renewal, since the pricing page’s only route past the cap is Enterprise+.

news.title: Attio replaced Enterprise’s custom quote with a self-serve Ultra plan
news.gist: Attio swapped its sales-quoted Enterprise tier for a self-serve Ultra plan with a fixed monthly credit allowance, which PricingSaaS reads as a move to self-serve at the top end and toward selling usage and governance separately.
points: Overages and SSO, SCIM and audit-log governance are now paid add-ons rather than parts of a negotiated quote
New table rows cover SQL access through API or MCP, data connectors and session management
The article can’t say whether existing Enterprise contracts move to the new price
It is the first pricing restructure Pulse has recorded for Attio
nums: monthly price of the new Ultra plan
workspace credits a month included in Ultra

100 days

news.why: Enterprise buyers renewing with Attio can now benchmark a quote against the listed Ultra price, but should model credit overages and governance add-ons, which are billed on top.

news.title: Pika launched Creator Team and Pro Team plans
news.gist: Pika added seat-priced team plans with pooled credits on top of its credit-based individual plans, a hybrid PricingSaaS says many AI tools are trying so that revenue grows with both headcount and usage.
points: Both team tiers need at least two paid seats, a minimum the author recommends copying
A single user still pays less on the existing individual Creator or Pro plan
Larger teams are sent to Enterprise, with custom credits and no listed seat price
The author flags that Pika’s individual credit caps have kept shrinking this month
nums: per seat a month for Creator Team, with 5,200 shared credits
per seat a month for Pro Team, with 17,100 shared credits

pricing changes at Pika in the last 90 days
news.why: Small teams buying Pika should compare the pooled team credits with two individual plans, since a shared pool only helps when usage is uneven across people.

news.title: Pricing Changes: November 9–15, 2026
news.gist: AgentDeals’ digest for our week has few direct price moves: E2B halved free concurrent sandboxes and Cloudflare for Startups stopped covering Workers AI for new members, while Bitrise opened its free Hobby plan to whole teams.
points: Google said Gemini 4 Carbon’s introductory rates end on 30 Nov, with every rate doubling from December
Val Town, Gadget, Sourcegraph Cody and Netlify Visual Editor all announced shutdowns or end of life
Several small API tools raised free request allowances but barred commercial use on their free plans
GitHub Copilot is deprecating six models in December
nums: Gemini 4 Carbon standard input price per million tokens from 1 Dec, double the introductory rate
concurrent sandboxes on E2B’s free Hobby plan, down from 20
monthly build minutes on Bitrise Hobby, which used to give 300 credits
top Workers AI cap that existing Cloudflare startup members keep until 1 Dec
news.why: If you call Gemini 4 Carbon, budget for double the per-token cost from December, and don’t count on startup credits to cover AI usage without rechecking their terms.

news.title: Huggingface dropped NVIDIA H100 endpoints from its pricing table.
news.gist: Hugging Face removed its AWS H100 inference endpoints from the hardware price list and left the other rows unchanged, and PricingSaaS reads the delisting as a capacity signal that trackers watching only prices would miss.
points: Newer, larger GPU tiers stay listed, so the H100 looks retired rather than cut as a budget option
The page doesn’t say whether running deployments on that hardware are affected
Most removals Pulse sees trim perks from plans, so dropping a priced hardware tier is unusual
Only two of Hugging Face’s earlier tracked changes were removals, both in 2024
nums: hourly price range of the removed 1- to 8-GPU H100 configurations
feature-removal changes among the 3,196 Pulse tracked in 180 days
real pricing changes Pulse has tracked at Hugging Face since Nov 2023
news.why: If you run endpoints on a specific GPU type, confirm with the vendor that it stays available, since a row vanishing from the price list can be the first warning.

patterns.p: GPU clouds raised Blackwell and Hopper rates, and tools built on rented compute raised prices or delisted options. AI products that resell this compute tend to pass such rises on later as dearer credits or smaller allowances.

patterns.p: Vendors stopped treating AI as an unlimited perk and put a count on it: weekly quotas, credits or per-call overage. The real cost is often the upgrade the cap pushes. Most of these records come from PricingSaaS reports.

patterns.p: Seats are being reworked rather than retired: some vendors added seat plans, some swapped seats for per-job prices, and others changed who counts as a billable seat. Part of this rests on PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: More changes cost buyers money than saved it
stats_analysis.figNote: changes that cost buyers more vs less; the other 15 repackaged plans
stats_analysis.p: Increases led cuts by a clear margin. About half of all this week’s records come from PricingSaaS reports, including the steepest list-price rises at Cedreo, Rustici Software and Crowdin; our own captures leaned toward compute and usage rates.

stats_analysis.t: The larger companies leaned against buyers
stats_analysis.figNote: changes at tier 1 and 2 companies that cost buyers more
stats_analysis.p: All of these come from our own captures. Slack metered Slackbot, Canva billed every Business member a seat, and Runpod and Together AI raised GPU rates. Datadog’s NetFlow price fell and then rose back within days, so it shows up on both sides.

stats_analysis.figNote: changes that tightened vs loosened a plan limit
stats_analysis.p: Limits tightened about as often as they loosened, so a steady list price says little about which way a plan moved. Tightening hit free and AI allowances at E2B, Composio and Pika; loosening added AI messages or retention at Jimdo, Supabase and Ably. Several of these records are PricingSaaS reports.

stats_analysis.t: AI was in about a third of the changes
stats_analysis.figNote: changes involving AI features, models or compute
stats_analysis.p: The AI changes skewed toward costing more: compute rises, new credit meters and smaller free AI allowances. Gains such as Jimdo’s bigger message allowance and Together AI’s cheaper image models were smaller moves.

stats_analysis.t: Free plans moved in both directions
stats_analysis.p: Bitrise opened its Hobby plan to whole teams, Supabase kept free audit logs for longer and CloudFix let free users run its fixers for 30 days, while E2B halved free sandboxes and Composio cut free tool calls. All but CloudFix are our own captures.

stats_analysis.figNote: promotion records this week, against 72 pricing changes
stats_analysis.p: First-year discounts appeared at TidyCal, Topaz Labs and ON1, Pictory widened its sale to every plan, and Kinsta’s annual offer got weaker. Some promotion records come from PricingSaaS reports, and promo prices end, so check the renewal price before signing.

news_trends.t: Usage billing keeps spreading through AI features
news_trends.p: PricingSaaS’s 180-day count of credit and usage-billing changes has risen with each article that cites it (the definitions differ slightly), and this week Slack, Attio and Pika added quotas, overage meters and pooled credits. Linear is the counterexample, selling tokens at cost inside the seat.

news_trends.t: Compute and model rates keep climbing
news_trends.p: Since early October the stories have tracked GPU and model rates going up at fal, Together AI and now Gemini 4 Carbon, plus older hardware being delisted; launch-day cuts like Baseten’s are the main exception. This week our own captures saw Runpod, Together AI and Hedra raise GPU rates.

news_trends.p: AgentDeals’ digests have logged free tiers shrinking or closing almost every week since September, alongside a steady run of shutdowns. November has been gentler so far, but this week still paired Bitrise’s wider free plan with E2B’s halved sandboxes and Cloudflare dropping Workers AI from new startup credits.

news_trends.t: The seat survives, with new jobs attached
news_trends.p: Earlier pieces argued seats lose ground as agents do more of the work, yet vendors keep seats and change what rides on them: Linear bundles agent work into the seat and Pika adds seat-priced team plans with pooled credits. Seat changes are still a small share of all pricing moves.
